description: Create a comprehensive setup-vertex.sh script at infra/gcp/setup-vertex.sh that automates the complete GCP/Vertex AI setup from a brand-new account. The script must cover: project creation/selection, enabling all required APIs, creating a service account with correct IAM roles, setting up Vertex AI Search datastore and search engine/app, generating service account key JSON, creating Artifact Registry for Docker images, and outputting all the environment variables the backend needs.
steps: Create infra/gcp/setup-vertex.sh as an executable bash script with clear section headers and comments

Section 1 - Configuration Variables: Define user-editable variables at the top: PROJECT_ID, BILLING_ACCOUNT_ID, REGION (default us-central1), DATASTORE_LOCATION (default global), DATASTORE_DISPLAY_NAME (default syrabit-edu-datastore), SERVICE_ACCOUNT_NAME (default syrabit-backend-sa), SEARCH_ENGINE_ID
Section 2 - Project Setup: Create GCP project (gcloud projects create) or select existing (gcloud config set project). Link billing account.

Section 3 - Enable APIs: Enable discoveryengine.googleapis.com, aiplatform.googleapis.com, run.googleapis.com, artifactregistry.googleapis.com, cloudbuild.googleapis.com, iam.googleapis.com, serviceusage.googleapis.com

Section 4 - Service Account: Create service account, assign roles: roles/discoveryengine.editor, roles/aiplatform.user, roles/run.developer, roles/artifactregistry.writer, roles/logging.logWriter, roles/monitoring.metricWriter

Section 5 - Vertex AI Search Datastore: Create a Discovery Engine datastore using the REST API (curl to discoveryengine.googleapis.com) since gcloud does not yet have full CLI support for datastore creation. Use the schema from infra/gcp/vertex-search-schema.json.
Section 6 - Search Engine/App: Create a Discovery Engine search engine that references the datastore using REST API
Section 7 - Artifact Registry: Create a Docker repository for Cloud Run images (REGION-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/syrabit/backend)
Section 8 - Service Account Key: Generate JSON key (gcloud iam service-accounts keys create), output the path and note it maps to GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON env var

Section 9 - Output Summary: Print all environment variables needed for .env file: VERTEX_PROJECT_ID, VERTEX_SEARCH_DATASTORE_ID, VERTEX_SEARCH_SERVING_CONFIG, VERTEX_SEARCH_LOCATION, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON (path to key file), VERTEX_GEMINI_MODEL, VERTEX_LOCATION
Include error handling (set -euo pipefail), color output for progress messages, and a prerequisites check (gcloud installed, authenticated, billing account available)
Add a --dry-run flag that prints commands without executing them
acceptance_criteria: infra/gcp/setup-vertex.sh exists and passes bash -n syntax validation
Script enables all APIs needed by the backend (discoveryengine, aiplatform, run, artifactregistry, cloudbuild)
Script creates service account with all roles needed for Discovery Engine search, Vertex AI Gemini, and Cloud Run
Script creates a Discovery Engine datastore using REST API with proper schema
Script creates a search engine/app linked to the datastore
Script generates service account key and outputs all env vars from apps/backend/app/config.py that relate to Vertex/GCP
Script has clear comments explaining each step
Script includes prerequisites check and error handling
verification: Confirm the script references all Vertex-related config vars from config.py
findings: Script passes bash -n syntax validation. All 7 env vars from config.py are output. All 7 APIs enabled. All 6 IAM roles assigned. Datastore and search engine created via REST API. Script is idempotent (checks for existing resources). --dry-run flag works via run_cmd wrapper and conditional blocks for REST API calls.
